messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT: GPU pool 'west-eu-gpu-pool' token-queue growth detected. queue_length=12k (+3000 in 5m), autoscaler attempted 3 scale actions but hit soft limit. Possible reduced effective capacity. Pager: @maya (oncall)

oncall-bot: Symptoms: high queue, increased latency, token rejects, some drivers reporting CUDA Xid entries. Severity: P2 -> escalated to P1 on metric breach.

maya (oncall): I'm pulling logs now. @sanjay can you check autoscaler logs? I'm seeing a bunch of OOMs on nodes and repeated driver restarts.

sanjay: on it. quick snapshot from autoscaler: `scale_attempts: [+4, +2, +0] reasons: quota, driver-failure` looks like we're capped by a policy (reserved cap + safety margin).

eli: I see node flaps in the last 6m, GPU driver unloading then kernel Xid 45/31 spamming. sample from node-az3-gn-12: ```
[ 2026-03-15T09:12:21Z ] nvlddmkm: Xid 31, PID 2876
[ 2026-03-15T09:12:23Z ] GPU memory allocation failed: OutOfMemory
[ 2026-03-15T09:12:24Z ] kubelet: container runtime restarted
```

infra-sre: Autoscaler blocked because of `max_nodes_per_pool=120` and pool already at 118; plus `driver_failure_rate` policy tripped. We need either to allow temporary burst or remove noisy nodes.

maya (oncall): Customer-impact? any 5xxs? CS?

customer-success: We have 2 active customers reporting degraded responses in prod (chat latency >10s). One support ticket opened: #CS-4127. A few more beta customers seeing token truncation.

maya (oncall): OK marking P1. Live mitigation plan: 1) throttle non-critical batch jobs 2) enable autoscaler burst to +20 nodes for 15m 3) reboot most-failing drivers on node-az3-gn-* 4) temporarily route heavy requests to fallback small-model pool. Anyone object?

eli: Agree. I'll run driver soft-restart on the flapping nodes and isolate the nodes showing repeated Xid 31. Command: ```
# list suspects
kubectl -n gpu get pods -l pool=west-eu-gpu -o wide | grep CrashLoop
# soft-restart driver on host
ssh root@node-az3-gn-12 'systemctl restart nvidia-driver' 
```

sanjay: I'll patch autoscaler policy to allow burst: `kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: infra/v1
kind: AutoscalerPolicy
metadata:
  name: west-eu-burst-allow
spec:
  max_burst_nodes: 20
  burst_duration_seconds: 900
EOF` then trigger scale. Doing in 30s.

ops-tools-bot: RUNBOOK: GPU-POOL-DEGRADATION - https://wiki.redwood/gpu-runbooks#pool-degradation. Recommended steps 1-7.

maya (oncall): I'm going to cordon node-az3-gn-12 and drain batch pods. Will update when done.

eli: found kernel log snippet that suggests a bad driver build shipped in last kernel-default rollout at 02:00 UTC. Patch level is `nvidia-525.85-rc2` on failing nodes. Other nodes have `nvidia-525.85`. Mismatch maybe causing runtime instability.

infra-sre: If it's a driver artifact, we should stop autoscaling into that image. Are images tagged per-driver?

Sanjay: yes, pool has mixed driver tags due to rolling update. I'll pin new nodes to `nvidia-525.85` and set `allow_mixed_drivers=false` temporarily. Applying now.

pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged by maya (oncall). Handoff ETA 30m.

maya (oncall): Live mitigation status: cordoned 3 nodes (az3-gn-12/15/16), drained 2 batch jobs, enabled burst policy. Kicking a controlled restart of 5 nodes one at a time.

customer-success: Notifying impacted customers: Messaged #CS-4127 with ETA ~15m for partial relief.

eli: After driver pin and restarts, node-az1/gn-02 shows stable GPU usage. Queue draining started, token rejects dropped by 40% in 7m.

infra-sre: Autoscaler just increased pool by +18 nodes, brought us to 136 effective nodes (temporary above hard target). Monitoring for spike.

maya (oncall): Observability note: increased tail latency for generation requests is correlated with nodes returning `Xid 31`. Setting a temporary filter to route requests with seq_len>1024 to small-model-pool.```

sanjay: Quick config snippet to route via dispatch service:
```
PATCH /v1/dispatch/config
{
  "routes": [{"match": "seq_len>1024", "target": "small-model-pool", "weight": 1}]
}
```

eli: After routing change, high-latency requests dropped 60% and queue length trending down. No new Xid reports in the last 6m on restarted nodes.

maya (oncall): Customer impact assessment: ~5% of production requests delayed >5s for ~20mins; two support tickets opened, one escalated. Recommend postmortem and mitigation credits for affected customers.

infra-sre: Root cause hypothesis: mixed driver rollout produced a driver/kernel mismatch -> runtime instability -> node flaps -> autoscaler hit soft limits -> queue growth -> customer impact.

maya (oncall): Next steps: 1) stabilize drivers (complete successful pin + rollout revert) 2) run health-check sweep across all pools for driver consistency 3) follow up with postmortem owner (eli) 4) review autoscaler soft limits and burst policies (sanjay) 5) notify engineering leadership.

eli: I'll own the postmortem and start drafting. Will include timelines, logs, config diffs, and customer impact.

sanjay: I'll open a ticket to relax `max_nodes_per_pool` or make emergency-burst automatic in similar failures.

maya (oncall): Handoff: I'm stepping out in 20m, handing to @eli for the long-running cleanup. Pagerduty updated. If anything regresses, ping @maya and @sanjay.

pagerduty-bot: Handoff complete: new assignee eli.

ops-tools-bot: NOTE: schedule a postmortem within 72 hours and include CS in follow-up.

eli: Logging final note here before I take over: queue length now 2.1k, token rejects at baseline. Rebooting remaining flagged nodes in a staggered fashion. Will post postmortem link when ready.

maya (oncall): Thanks team :heart: Great coordination.

customer-success: We'll keep customers updated and share remediation notes. Thanks.
